3.title: CommitFusion Examples
3.content: This guide provides practical examples for using CommitFusion cmdlets. All examples follow the Conventional Commits specification.

5.title: New-Commit Examples
5.content: Basic Usage . Generate a simple chore commit: . New-Commit -Type chore -Description "Update dependencies" . Output: . 🔧 chore: Update dependencies . Documentation Commits . Create a documentation commit with notes and footer: . $params = @{ Type = "docs" Description = "Update API documentation" Scope = "api" Notes = @("Added authentication examples", "Fixed typos") GitUser = "sgkens" Footer = $true } New-Commit @params . Output: . 📝 docs(api): Update API documentation 🧳 Notes: - Added authentication examples - Fixed typos 👤 @sgkens 📅 7:48PM, Thursday 2th October 2025 . Bug Fix Commits . Create a bug fix commit with scope and fixes: . New-Commit -Type fix -Description "Fix memory leak" -Scope "#234" -BugFixes "Memory leak in authentication handler" . Output: . 🐛 fix(#234): Fix memory leak 🧰 Build: patch 🐛 BUGFIXES: 🦠 Memory leak in authentication handler ..🖊 . Feature Commits . Add a new feature with multiple components: . $featureParams = @{ Type = "feat" Description = "Add OAuth support" Scope = "auth" Notes = @("Requires API key", "Rate limited to 1000 requests/hour") FeatureAdditions = @( "OAuth 2.0 authentication flow", "Token refresh mechanism" ) GitUser = "sgkens" Footer = $true } New-Commit @featureParams .

6.title: Working with Changelogs
6.content: Update Changelog with New Commit . # Create and update changelog in one pipeline New-Commit @params | Format-FusionMD | Update-Changelog -LogFile changelog.md . Commit Types and Versioning . List all major version change types: . Get-CISetFusion -Major . List all patch version change types: . Get-CISetFusion -Patch .

10.title: Complete Pipeline Example
10.content: Here’s a complete example showing all features working together: . $commitParams = @{ Type = "feat" Description = "Implement OAuth2" Scope = "auth" Notes = @( "Requires environment configuration", "Updates security policy" ) FeatureAdditions = @( "OAuth2 authentication flow", "Automatic token refresh" ) GitUser = "sgkens" Footer = $true } New-Commit @commitParams | Format-FusionMD | Update-Changelog -LogFile changelog.md | Set-Commit .

12.title: CommitFusion Features
12.content: CommitFusion implements the Conventional Commits specification with enhanced features including notes, feature tracking, and emoji support via gitmoji.

13.title: Core Features
13.content: 🔄 Git Integration . | Seamless commit application with Set-Commit | Automatic Git user information retrieval | Repository state validation | Changelog management | . ⚡ PowerShell Integration . | Rich tab completion for commit types | Strict parameter validation | Full pipeline support | PSScriptAnalyzer compliance | . 🎨 Enhanced Commit Messages . CommitFusion generates structured commit messages with the following components: . 📝 type(scope): description 🏗️ Build: semver 📋 Notes: - Note details - Additional information ✨ Feature Additions: - New feature 1 - New feature 2 🐛 Bug Fixes: - Fix description - Issue resolution ⚠️ Breaking Changes: - Major change 1 - Migration notes 👤 @username 📅 timestamp . 📊 Version Management . Automatic semantic versioning based on commit types: . | Type | Version Bump | Example | . | breaking | major | 1.0.0 → 2.0.0 | . | feat | minor | 1.0.0 → 1.1.0 | . | fix | patch | 1.0.0 → 1.0.1 | .

14.title: Advanced Features
14.content: 📝 Markdown Integration . | Convert commits to Markdown format | Automatic changelog updates | Custom template support | Pipeline-friendly formatting | . 🎯 Semantic Version Analysis . Get-GitAutoVersion analyzes commit history to determine version increments: . | Major: Breaking changes (resets minor & patch) | Minor: New features (resets patch) | Patch: Bug fixes and small changes | . 🎨 Emoji Support . Two comprehensive emoji collections: . | Gitmoji Integration . | Standard git-specific emojis | Based on gitmojis schema | . | Unicode Emoji Support . | Full unicode emoji catalog | Sourced from unicode.org | . | .

15.title: Usage Example
15.content: New-Commit -Type feat -Description "Add OAuth support" ` -Scope auth ` -Notes "Requires API key" ` -FeatureAdditions @( "OAuth 2.0 flow", "Token refresh" ) | Format-FusionMD | Update-Changelog . Back to top Installing CommitFusion .

18.title: Get-CiSet
18.content: . Get-CiSet parses 🧷carloscuesta gitmojis Schema JSON file and return as a PSObject, making it helpful if you wish to utilize custom types in your commit messages. The $moduleroot/libs/Gitmojis.json file serves as a reference, but you have the flexibility to customize it according to your preferences, as long as the schema remains consistent. Additionally, it’s worth noting that the type and cfa additions are the same as those found in the $moduleroot/libs/CommitFusion.types.json file. 🟢 Syntax . Get-CiSet . 🟠 Parameter List . | None | . 🟣 For Example: . Get-CiSet | Select-Object -First 10 | FT -Wrap . 🟣 Will Output: . name description semver code entity emoji ---- ----------- ------ ---- ------ ----- art Improve structure / format of the code. :art: &#x1f3a8; 🎨 zap Improve performance. patch :zap: &#x26a1; ⚡️ fire Remove code or files. :fire: &#x1f525; 🔥 bug Fix a bug. patch :bug: &#x1f41b; 🐛 ambulance Critical hotfix. patch :ambulance: &#128657; 🚑️ sparkles Introduce new features. minor :sparkles: &#x2728; ✨ memo Add or update documentation. :memo: &#x1f4dd; 📝 rocket Deploy stuff. :rocket: &#x1f680; 🚀 lipstick Add or update the UI and style files. patch :lipstick: &#ff99cc; 💄 tada Begin a project. :tada: &#127881; 🎉 .

19.title: Get-CommitTypes
19.content: . Get-CommitTypes* Takes 4 optional Parameters, it will parse and write to console the types from the $moduleroot/libs/commitFusion.types.json file. The types can be further filtered by the following parameters: . 🟢 Syntax . Get-CommitTypes [-NoSemver] [-Major] <switch> [-Minor] <switch> [-Patch] <switch> . 🟠 Parameter List . 🔴Required Parameter 🔘Optional Parameter . | Required | Parameter Name | Type | Description | . | 🔘 | NoSemver | [switch] | Filters types without semantic versioning. | . | 🔘 | Major | [switch] | Filters types of major version changes. | . | 🔘 | Minor | [switch] | Filters types of minor version changes. | . | 🔘 | Patch | [switch] | Filters types of patch version changes. | . If no parameters are specified, it will return all the types. If you would like to return the PSObject as this function renders the result using Spectre.Console via SimpleSpectreWrapper, you can use the -raw parameter to return the PSObject instead. Type description semver cfa emoji ---- ----------- ------ --- ----- changes Introduce breaking changes. major {@{action=}} 💥 feat Introduce new features. minor {@{action=}} ✨ fix Fixed bugs. patch {@{action=}} 🐛 docs Update Documentation. {@{action=}} 📝 style Update style. patch {@{action=}} 💄 perf Improve performance. patch {@{action=}} ⚡️ test Add tests. {@{action=}} ✅ build Build. patch {@{action=}} 📦 ci Continuous integration. {@{action=}} 👷 chore Tooling, Generic commit {@{action=}} 🔧 revert Revert changes. patch {@{action=}} ⏪ bookmark Release / Version tags. {@{action=}} 🔖 wip Work in progress. {@{action=}} 🚧 gitignore Add or update a .gitignore file. {@{action=}} 🙈 flag Add, update, or remove feature flags. {@{action=}} 🚩 improve Improve structure / format of the code. patch {@{action=}} 🎨 hotfix Critical hotfix. patch {@{action=}} 🚑️ deploy Deploy stuff. {@{action=}} 🚀 project Begin a project. {@{action=}} 🎉 security Fix security issues. patch {@{action=}} 🔒️ refactor Refactor code. {@{action=}} ♻️ depadd Add a dependency. patch {@{action=}} ➕ depdell Remove a dependency. patch {@{action=}} ➖ config Add or update configuration files. patch {@{action=}} 🔧 typos Fix typos. patch {@{action=}} ✏️ resources Move or rename resources (e.g.: files, paths, routes). {@{action=}} 🚚 fix-s Simple fix for a non-critical issue. patch {@{action=}} 🩹 deadcode Remove dead code. {@{action=}} ⚰️ Depre Remove deprecate code. {@{action=}} 🗑️ concurrency Add or update code related to multithreading or concurrency. {@{action=}} 🧵 Infra Infrastructure related changes. patch {@{action=}} 🧱 . Note! You can modify the $moduleroot/libs/CommitFusion.json file to add your own types, using the GitMojis. See New-Commit Types for more information.

21.title: Overview
21.content: Gets emojis from either the GitMojis.json or miscmojis.json configuration files. You can retrieve all emojis of a specific type or search for a particular emoji by name.

23.title: Parameters
23.content: | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | . | -Type | String | Yes | Specifies the emoji collection to use: either miscmojis or gitmojis | . | -Name | String | No | The name of the specific emoji to return. If omitted, returns all emojis of the specified type | .

24.title: Examples
24.content: Example 1: Get a specific Git emoji . Get-Emoji -Type gitmojis -Name bug . Returns the bug emoji from the gitmojis collection. Example 2: List all miscellaneous emojis . Get-Emoji -Type miscmojis . Returns all emojis from the miscmojis collection.

25.title: Notes
25.content: . | The emoji collections are stored in JSON format | Case-insensitive search is supported for the -Name parameter | Returns $null if no matching emoji is found | .

28.title: CommitFusion
28.content: A PowerShell module that simplifies generating Conventional Commit Messages for git repositories. Get Started View on GitHub .

29.title: Overview
29.content: CommitFusion helps you create standardized commit messages that follow the Conventional Commits specification. The module enhances the standard by including additional sections: . | 📝 Notes | ✨ Feature Notes | ➕ Feature Additions | 🔧 Fixes | 🐛 Bug Fixes | ❗ Breaking Changes | 👤 Footer (with GitUser and timestamp) | . Additionally, CommitFusion integrates modified gitmoji support to add visual context to your commits, if Emotocons are not your thing simply disable them, via New-Commit -NoEmojis paramete. or by use the dedicated cmdlets Enable-CommitFusionEmojis and Disable-CommitFusionEmojis. before using New-Commit or Set-Commit respectively.

30.title: Quick Start
30.content: 1. Installation . Install directly from the PowerShell Gallery: . Install-Module -Name 'CommitFusion' -Scope CurrentUser Import-Module CommitFusion . 2. Basic Usage . View available commit types: . Get-CommitTypes . Generate a commit message: . New-Commit -Type 'feat' -Scope 'ui' -Description 'add new dashboard component' -Notes 'Implemented responsive design' . Commit changes with the generated message: . New-Commit -Type 'fix' -Scope 'api' -Description 'resolve authentication issue' -Notes 'Fixed token validation' | Set-Commit -Confirm .

Additional types can be added to ./moduleroot/libs/CommitFustion.types.json file if needed. Schema follows Gitmojis Schema, gitmoji.dev with additional type and cfa added to the object array items. 37.title: Set-Commit
37.content: . Set-Commit takes 2 Optional Parameters, will simple run git commit -m $commitmessage and will use the output from New-Commit as the commit message. | You are in a git repository | You have staged files | . 🟢 Syntax . Set-commit [-AsStringForCommit <string>] [-Test] <switch> [-Confirm] <switch> . 🟠 Parameter List . 🔴Required Parameter 🔘Optional Parameter . | Required | Parameter Name | Type | Description | . | 🔘 | Test | [switch] | Display Test if specified will output Test. | . | 🔘 | Confirm | [switch] | Display Confirm if specified will output Confirm. | . 🟣 For Example: . New-Commit -Type feat -Description "Updated module logic" | Set-Commit -Confirm -confirm .

38.title: Update-ChangeLog
38.content: . Takes the output of Format-FustionMD and appends it to the Changelog File. 🟢 Syntax . Update-ChangeLog [-logfile] <string> . 🟠 Parameter List . 🔴Required Parameter 🔘Optional Parameter . | Required | Parameter Name | Type | Description | . | 🔴 | logfile | [string] | The relative path to the changelog file. If not specified, it will look for CHANGELOG.md in the current directory. If the file is not found, it will create one. The function will attempt to pre-pend the output from Format-FusionMD to the file. | . 🟣 For Example: . New-Commit -Type feat ` -Description "Added new feature" ` -Scope "add" ` -Notes "Note 1","Note 2" ` -BugFixes "BugFixes 1","BugFixes 2" ` -FeatureNotes "FeatureNotes 1","FeatureNotes 2" ` -FeatureAddtions "FeatureAddtions 1","FeatureAddtions 2" ` -BreakingChanges "BreakingChanges 1","BreakingChanges 2" ` -GitUser "GitUser" ` -GitGroup "GitGroup" ` -Footer | Format-FusionMD | Update-ChangeLog -logfile "CHANGELOG.md" .
